props.title: Same Shape, New Names

B01.capture_spec: C01: custom scene 'pad on a flat square' (CAPTURE-PLAN S1): lab-shaders/12-signal-pad.gdshader on a 1.55 x 1.55 QuadMesh lying flat, orthographic camera size 2.6 from (5.8, 9, 11) toward the origin, activation 0 to 1 across 0 to 0.86 of the clip then held at 1 (the clip is as long as the longer of its two beats), 30 fps, Forward+, stage #D9D5CA. Frame at the 50 % mark reads activation 0.5 (mid-tone), at 85 % reads 0.85.
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'Same Shape, New Names' (serif 40) top-left. Left: the ten-line pad shader on a cream code card, no line focus. Right: a framed window holding a real Godot render of a flat square lying flat, seen from the game's camera angle, charging from striped rust-brown to flat green as activation climbs. Caption: 'a shader from a small game'.
B01.motion_claim: The square charges from striped rust to flat green while its ten lines of code sit beside it.

show.event: striped rust square, code card beside it
half charged: greener, stripes fading
flat green

B01.runner_up: manim drawing of a pad charging
B01.why: A real render is the honest picture of the payoff, and the viewer sees the whole effect and its whole source at once; a drawing would only claim it.

B02.visual_intent: The compiled skeleton file lab-shaders/03-skeleton-3d.gdshader drawn as a cream code card (Menlo, 12 lines). Brackets draw in on the voice's words and each carries a one-word label: 'a first line' brackets line 1 (label 'type'), 'up to three functions' brackets lines 5 to 12, the three empty functions (label 'functions'), 'dials' brackets line 3 where a small dial (a circle with a turning tick) sits at the card's right (label 'dials'). Caption at the top, GLOSSARY wording: 'shader: a small program the graphics card runs to decide how something is drawn'.
B02.motion_claim: A dot steps down the lines like a program, then three brackets draw in one after another, each with its label, and a small dial turns.

show.event: card and shader caption; a terracotta dot steps down the lines like a program counter
bracket 1: type
bracket 2: functions
bracket 3 and the turning dial

B02.why: Brackets growing around real code show the SHAPE (the parts and their order), which paced line focus alone cannot.

B03.visual_intent: The line `shader_type canvas_item;` in Menlo over a flat teal square (outline icon). On the cue the word canvas_item slides out and spatial slides in, while the flat square turns into an isometric cube in the same teal with faint triangle edges; a one-word label 'mesh' points at the cube. Caption, GLOSSARY wording: 'shader type: the first line; says what the shader is for'.
B03.motion_claim: The word canvas_item is replaced by spatial and the flat square turns into a cube.

show.event: first line over the flat square
spatial replaces canvas_item; square becomes a cube (starts after the midpoint, so the 50 % frame is the settled first line over the flat square)
'mesh' label on the cube

B03.why: Two worlds, each with its own first line, is the contrast the sentence names; a replaced word plus a square that becomes a cube says it with motion.

B04.visual_intent: Left: the test rectangle (a flat square) with four terracotta corner dots. Right: a 12-by-8 pixel grid of outline cells with the square's footprint over it. The four dots flash in order with a counter 1 to 4 and the label 'vertex()'; the covered cells tint one by one, each with a tiny 'fragment()' tag, then all hold; a small lamp icon (drawn bulb with rays) appears and the covered cells brighten once per lamp, two lamps in turn, with the label 'light()'. Captions, GLOSSARY wording: 'vertex: a corner point of a shape' and 'pixel: one dot of the picture on screen'.
B04.motion_claim: Four dots flash in turn, then the covered cells tint one by one, then the cells brighten once for each lamp.

show.event: square with four dots; both captions
dots flash 1 to 4
covered cells tint one by one
lamp 1 then lamp 2 brighten the cells

B04.why: 'Once for each vertex', 'once for each pixel' and 'once per light' are counts; four dots, a tinting grid and two lamps are those counts as motion.

B05.visual_intent: Two code cards, lab-shaders/01-flat-teal-2d.gdshader at left and lab-shaders/02-flat-teal-3d.gdshader at right (Menlo, 5 lines each), the same positions line for line. The first lines already differ (canvas_item and spatial: label 'type', the idea of the previous beat). On the cues the changed pieces get a terracotta ring in turn: 'COLOR' becomes 'ALBEDO' as the voice says 'the output' (label 'output'); a short ring goes round the four numbers of the two-D color as the voice says 'four numbers'; as it says 'and alpha' the ring moves to the last number, 1.0, and a caption lands, GLOSSARY wording: 'alpha: how visible a pixel is: 0 invisible, 1 solid'; as it says 'three numbers' 'vec4(' becomes 'vec3(' and ', 1.0' dissolves (label 'three numbers'); as it says 'Alpha becomes a separate output' a small 'ALPHA' chip appears beside the card. The unchanged text stays still.
B05.motion_claim: The output and the number of numbers change in turn while everything else stays exactly where it was.

show.event: both cards side by side; the first lines differ (label 'type')
COLOR becomes ALBEDO; label 'output'
a short ring round the four numbers of the two-D color (done by 0.44)
the ring moves to the last number, 1.0; the alpha caption lands
vec4 becomes vec3 and ', 1.0' dissolves; label 'three numbers'
an 'ALPHA' chip appears beside the card: alpha is its own output

B05.why: Most of the two programs is identical; a morph that moves only three tokens is the claim 'same shape, new names' made visible.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · two flat squares · scripted hand-over

B07.capture_spec: C18: custom scene 'wrong type' (CAPTURE-PLAN S6): two QuadMesh 1.4 x 1.4 at x -0.95 and +0.95 on the stage, no WorldEnvironment and no lamp (as verify8); both start with no material; at 0.12 of the clip the scene script gives the left lab-shaders/18-two-d-shader-on-a-mesh.gdshader and the right lab-shaders/19-three-d-shader-on-a-mesh.gdshader as material_override (--call-at); the clip is as long as the beat; orthographic size 2.6; Forward+. Verified: no engine error; left stays (0.612, 0.600, 0.569) (the no-material look), right reads (1.0, 0.0, 0.0).
B07.visual_intent: A wide result strip (layout 'stack': result above, and under it a one-line excerpt, the two-D shader's first line `shader_type canvas_item;`, with a tag on that line: 'canvas_item: shaders for 2D and UI'). Real Godot render: two flat squares side by side, both plain grey at first. At the hand-over (0.12 of the clip, as the voice says 'Give a three-D mesh a two-D shader') each is given a red shader: the left one gets the canvas_item shader above, the right one a spatial shader that paints red. The right square turns red; the left stays exactly as it was. Labels land under them: 'canvas_item: ignored' and 'spatial: red'.
B07.motion_claim: Both squares are handed a red shader; only the right one changes.

show.event: two plain grey squares
first line focused; the shaders are handed over; the right square turns red
'canvas_item: ignored' label on the left square
'spatial: red' label on the right

B07.why: A non-event is hard to show; two squares given the same instruction, one of which visibly does nothing, makes it visible, and the empty log is told in words.

props.caption: UV: a point's address on the shape: 0 to 1 across, 0 to 1 down

B08.capture_spec: C02: custom scene 'three meshes' (CAPTURE-PLAN S2): lab-shaders/06-uv-colors-3d.gdshader on QuadMesh 1x1 (x -1.35), BoxMesh 1x1x1 (x 0), SphereMesh r 0.5 (x +1.35); each swings about Y by plus or minus 50 deg (a sine, period 8 s) with a fixed -20 deg tilt about X (NOT a full turn: with default culling the flat square vanishes while its back faces the camera, verify9 run 9a); orthographic size 2.6; the clip is as long as the beat; 30 fps; Forward+. Verified mesh data: quad UV (0,0) top-left; box 3 x 2 cells; sphere U wraps once.
B08.visual_intent: A wide result strip (layout 'stack': result above, and under it a one-line excerpt: line 5 of the six-line shader, `ALBEDO = vec3(UV.x, UV.y, 0.0);`, with a tag 'red = UV.x (across), green = UV.y (down)'). Real Godot render: a flat square, a box and a sphere in a row, all swinging side to side about the vertical axis (plus or minus 50 degrees, one swing in eight seconds), every one painted with red-across, green-down address colors. The square shows the whole red-green gradient, the box shows a different patch on each face, the sphere wraps its map around itself. One-word labels land under them: 'square', 'box', 'sphere'. Caption, GLOSSARY wording: 'UV: a point's address on the shape: 0 to 1 across, 0 to 1 down'.
B08.motion_claim: The colors stay glued to each surface as the meshes swing, and each mesh shows a different map.

show.event: three meshes turning
ALBEDO line highlighted
'square' label
'box' label
'sphere' label

B08.why: Real renders show that UV is glued to the surface and differs per mesh; the swing is the proof, and a drawing could only illustrate it.

B09.visual_intent: Three boxes slide in left to right and link: a cube icon over 'mesh instance', then 'ShaderMaterial', then 'shader' (a small file icon marked .gdshader). The link between the first two carries a small tab 'material override'. A dot travels from the shader back to the mesh instance (meaning: look here). Captions: 'mesh instance: the node that draws a mesh' (docs: MeshInstance3D is the main node that draws a mesh) and, GLOSSARY wording, 'ShaderMaterial: a material that holds your shader and its settings'.
B09.motion_claim: Each box slides in as it is named, the slot tab lands on the first link, and the dot travels back to the node.

B09.why: Three nested things is a structure with a shape, and a drawn chain with a travelling dot shows it without claiming an Inspector label or layout this film did not capture; the property name material_override is run-verified, and a real frame is the labelled upgrade if an editor driver exists.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · one lamp · scripted lamp switch

B10.capture_spec: C03a: custom scene 'lamp' (CAPTURE-PLAN S3), one sphere: lab-shaders/02-flat-teal-3d.gdshader on a SphereMesh r 0.5 at the origin, orthographic size 1.8; white ambient light energy 0.25; one DirectionalLight3D tilted 30 deg down at yaw -65 deg, switched off until 0.56 of the clip and on from then (scripted switch, held there); Forward+. Verified: lamp off, the sphere reads one dim value everywhere (0.337, 0.435, 0.412); lamp on at -65 deg, the left side reads about 0.65 to 0.68 red and the right 0.337 (verify4, verify10).
B10.visual_intent: Left: the five-line shader (ALBEDO = vec3(0.37, 0.64, 0.57)) with its ALBEDO line focused. Right: a real Godot render of one teal sphere, centred. At first the lamp is off and the sphere is a flat dim disc (the 'flat teal disc' the voice says you might expect). At the reveal the lamp switches on, from the upper left: bright on one side, dim on the other, and it stays that way. Labels land on the sphere: 'bright', then 'dim'; a 'lamp' tag lands in the upper left as the voice names the scene's lamp.
B10.motion_claim: A flat dim disc becomes a sphere with a bright side and a dim side the moment the lamp switches on, although the code names one flat color.

show.event: ALBEDO line focused; the sphere is a flat dim disc (lamp off)
lamp switches on at yaw -65 degrees; 'bright' label
'dim' label
'lamp' tag in the upper left

B10.why: A real render makes the surprise honest: nothing in the code says 'shade', and the sphere is shaded.
